jobs.title: 2027 Investment Associate Intern
jobs.description:
For 50 years, Bridgewater has pursued one idea: the world can be understood. Markets and economies follow cause-and-effect relationships—and by understanding them, we think we can beat the markets and generate true uncorrelated returns ("alpha") at significant scale. Our clients include some of the world’s most sophisticated institutional investors who turn to us to use our unique insights to solve their biggest problems.

Generating alpha at scale is an exceptionally difficult task.  It requires predicting the future and doing so better than the millions of other extremely smart, highly motivated people who are trying to do the same. Our investment strategies seek to understand and navigate macroeconomic shifts that drive the world’s most liquid markets (bonds, currencies, equities, commodities, credit). These shifts have a very limited sample size (some of them haven’t yet happened in our lifetimes).

Our approach is to start by digging deep to develop a fundamental cause-effect understanding  of the economic and financial relationships that drive markets.  We represent this understanding in a model of the world that we call our System —code and algorithms that generate views automatically, by ingesting vast amounts of significantly cleaned data and reflecting the relationships we’ve learned over decades of intense study and experience. Being systematic allows us to stress-test the quality of our ideas through time, and also helps ensure that at any given point, our positions reflect everything we’ve ever learned, so that our people can spend all their time focused on compounding on our understanding at a faster rate than markets are learning.

This approach requires us to be at the forefront of human-machine collaboration.  Since 2012, Bridgewater has aggressively pursued the vision of the artificial investor that can do everything a human can, with computers not just representing the insights but also generating the insights themselves.   In 2023, we introduced AIA (Artificial Investment Associate), our fully machine-powered investing strategy. Our learnings in building AIA are now transforming even our human investors’ jobs, allowing us to rapidly discover and systemize new insights, and accelerating our transformation toward a fully integrated system that combines the best of human and machine intelligence.

Every day we obsessively interrogate our systems against our independent investor insights, and work to evolve our systems to reflect how the world is changing.  Beating the markets with this approach requires intense collaboration  between brilliant people who constantly push themselves and each other to improve every week, to arrive at the best ideas without ego or politics.  We rapidly elevate the best thinkers to greater responsibility.

We are looking to hire great talent for our Investment Associate roles. Does this sound like you?

Our investment associates are the core team responsible for generating our macro and market insights, building our investment systems, and overseeing our portfolios. They are:

- Relentlessly, obsessively—curious.  To beat markets, you must have unique insight—but markets are always learning. We need individuals fiercely driven to understand how the world works, uncovering new logical relationships, testing and exploring new data sources, and consistently trying to expand their understanding and constantly improve.

- Deeply independent—bordering on iconoclastic—thinkers.  For decades, Bridgewater has been studying markets and economies and reflecting our best understanding in our investment systems. We need independent-minded individuals who will come in and tell us why what we’re doing and thinking is wrong—and be right about it.

- Conceptual and analytical.  We need people who are excited by both the challenge of understanding abstract concepts and the challenge of translating insights into quantifiable measures in a systematic investment process. We are looking for exceptionally bright, “high horsepower” thinkers.

- Able to draw insights from a wide variety of backgrounds.  Our investment approach draws from multiple disciplines—most obviously economics and finance—but also computer science, mathematics, statistics, political science, history, natural science, and more. To that end, our Investment Associates also come from a wide variety of backgrounds  and are also unusually flexible thinkers.

- People who love collaborating, have a ton of grit, and are determined to grow rapidly.  How we interact with each other is crucial to our success. The problems we must solve are so hard and multifaceted that they require continuous, intense collaboration and exploration of ideas. Grit is also essential—many of the problems we try to solve don’t have immediate or clear answers and wrestling through to the truth alongside others takes enormous perseverance. We need people who strive to constantly push themselves and each other to be their best and improve every week, to arrive at truth without ego or politics. If you prefer to work as an individual, this is not for you. If the pain of being pushed to evolve each day doesn’t excite you, this is not for you.

What do Investment Associates at Bridgewater do?

Investment Associates at Bridgewater cover a wide range of functions, and most tend to specialize in one or two areas. We need a wide range of people and capabilities to power our investment engine and take on the different responsibilities involved:

- Research the drivers of economies and markets.  Build the insights that underly our investment edge and stay on top of a constantly evolving world. Recent top research priorities have included understanding the implications of the shift to the new economic and geopolitical paradigm we call  modern mercantilism  and the macro implications of transformational advances in  artificial intelligence .

- Develop systematic indicators for trading markets.  For every insight we learn, we codify it in algorithms that run every day to process vast data on economic conditions and form views on markets. These algorithms represent one of the world’s most advanced and profitable expert system. It is critical that this system not just efficiently model the significant complexity of our understanding but also be exceptionally intelligible so that we can continually combine the best of human and machine intelligence.

- Oversee our portfolios and live and breathe the markets.  Reflecting human intuition into investment systems is an exceptionally difficult task, and some of our most impactful investment system improvements come from investors who are watching markets every day, independently forming views, and reconciling their views with the outputs of our investment systems. In many cases, our systems will also be reflecting a factor they are underweighing or forgot about (that’s the power of systemization), but in an important set of cases, our investors will be identifying dynamics that our systems are not currently able to capture, which then drives further evolution.

- Drive the future of human and machine investor collaboration.  Getting the most out of the collaboration between humans and machines has always been at the core of our systematic learning process, and we’ve continued to evolve our approach with the launch of AIA. We need investors who are exceptionally creative users of technology who will drive our transformation toward a fully integrated system that combines the best of human and machine intelligence. This includes a radical inflection in how rapidly we can learn about the world and systemize those ideas.

- Partnering with the world’s most sophisticated institutional investors.  At Bridgewater our clients are some of the biggest pools of capital on the planet. Many of the dynamics we wrestle with in our own investment strategies are the same concerns our clients are wrestling with. Building a relationship that goes beyond just the money we manage for our clients has been foundational to our business model since our origins. This includes writing the  Bridgewater Daily Observations , which provides an over-the-shoulder look into how we’re seeing the world, as well as conducting a number of custom research projects and building tailored portfolio solutions for our largest clients.

What can I expect in an Investment Associate summer internship?

Our goal is to provide interns with real and meaningful exposure to a fundamental and systematic investment process. As Investment Associates, we live and breathe markets and want our interns to have the chance to do the same. We hate the concept of “busy work” and try to make the internship as real of a window as possible. From the first week on, you’ll be expected to form your own macroeconomic and market views—including the opportunity to bet with your intern compensation and enter “positions” in actual markets Bridgewater trades, where Bridgewater will take the other side, using our in-house Investor Track Record tool.

The internship is structured around the same components as Bridgewater’s research and investment process—you’ll start by looking out at the world and perceiving the most important dynamics for investors related to a specific economy and market. You’ll then synthesize your key views. Finally, you’ll get exposure to systemization—taking your point-in-time views and working with our investors to translate the core logic into data and mathematical expressions that you can then stress-test through time.

Throughout the internship, you’ll also receive world-class markets and macroeconomic training via an abridged version of our first year Investment Associate class. This will cover the foundational frameworks, introduction to analytical methods we use in our research, and exposure to our technology stack. Our training ecosystem is designed so that anyone willing to put in the work can get the knowledge and skills they need to succeed in the internship and get a taste of what it’s like to be a real macro investor.

Compensation

Total compensation for this position is $71,000 for the 8-week internship (less applicable deductions and withholdings), including a sign on bonus. In addition, our compensation package includes housing.

Previously, we used to post separate job applications for Investment Associates and Investment Engineers. As we plan for a future where we’ll need both incredible independent investor insight and deep human-machine collaboration, we are consolidating those roles into a single Investment Associate position. As described above, the IA role will still require a wide variety of people from a range of different backgrounds, and there will be many different areas of potential focus that our IAs can specialize in.

Nothing in this job description constitutes an offer or guarantee of employment.

jobs.title: Client Investment Research Associate
jobs.description:
About Bridgewater

Bridgewater Associates is a premier asset management firm, focused on delivering unique return streams, insight and partnership for the most sophisticated global institutional investors.

Our investment process is driven by a tireless pursuit to understand how the world’s markets and economies work — using cutting-edge technology to validate and execute on timeless and universal investment principles.

Founded in 1975, we are a community of independent thinkers who share a commitment for excellence. By fostering a culture of openness, transparency, and inclusion, we strive to unlock the most complex questions in investment strategy, management, and corporate culture.

Explore more information about Bridgewater on our website  here .

Our Culture

Our culture is anchored in excellence, meaning constant improvement, and it is deeply tied to our mission. Because markets are objective, competitive, and getting smarter everyday, we need to keep rapidly improving to have any chance of beating them. Truth is our most essential tool for engaging with the markets and constantly improving because once you know what’s true about your problems and opportunities, you can determine how to get better. Valuing truth means being transparent about your decision-making and mistakes, giving and receiving feedback with humility, and fighting for the best answers over hierarchy, ego, or self-interest. Operating this way is hard – it’s only possible because we build meaning in our work and relationships. This meaning comes from the audacity of the mission, and the joy of working alongside people who make you a better version of yourself. The culture, like Bridgewater itself, is always evolving. In 1997 our founder Ray Dalio wrote down his lessons, starting with a  Philosophy Statement  which remains our foundation. This later evolved into a set of 300+ Principles. In 2022, when Ray transitioned the company, we re-underwrote several of those principles and evolved others, with a specific focus on  Meritocracy.  Today the culture sits, alongside our people, as our most important edge. When we get it right, it’s the engine that powers everything else.

Explore more information about Bridgewater’s culture on our website  here .

About Your Role

Bridgewater’s mission has always been to understand how the world works and translate that understanding into the best possible portfolios for our clients. The Client Investment Research Analyst role sits at the center of that translation. It is a role unlike others in asset management: you take Bridgewater’s view of the cause-and-effect linkages in economies and markets and put it to work advising the world’s most sophisticated institutional investors.

You will work on the investment problems facing Bridgewater’s institutional clients: sovereign wealth funds, large public pensions, endowments, and other major allocators. The work spans the full range of what these institutions need from a macro investment partner, from synthesizing what’s going on in the world, to considering how to best manage a portfolio from the perspective of each investors’ unique goals and constraints, both strategically and tactically. You will do this alongside Bridgewater’s Strategists, a small group of senior investors appointed by our co-CIOs to lead our work with allocators; as you develop, you will take on more of the investment content those engagements carry.

What the role builds.  Over time, you develop what we call proxy CIO judgment: the ability to stand in an institutional investor’s shoes, understand their full set of constraints and objectives, and form a view on how to manage their portfolio both strategically and in view of the macro environment today. You apply Bridgewater’s macro thinking to institutional portfolios and the constraints they operate within. You also develop a working understanding of how large allocators make decisions: their governance, return objectives, liability profiles, and strategic priorities.

Growth and career paths.  Analysts progress from building foundational skills through to independent investment practitioner and, for those who continue on the team, into senior leadership roles where they operate as close partners to Strategists. At the senior end, you will hold a view on Bridgewater’s synthesis of the macro environment and portfolio construction, as well as which investment content will most change how our clients think about their portfolios. The capabilities you build here open many paths across Bridgewater’s investment community over time. The specific path depends on your strengths, interests, and how your capabilities develop.

Day-to-day responsibilities include:

- Designing analytical approaches to complex investment questions and executing the research from framing through synthesis

- Partnering with Strategists, co-CIOs, and asset class research teams to develop investment content for client engagements

- Synthesizing Bridgewater’s macro outlook and translating it into investment narratives tailored to each institution’s context

- Developing independent views on markets, institutional asset allocation, and the macro environment to inform our work

- At senior levels: developing junior analysts, setting team quality standards, and contributing to broader investment research priorities

Interested in learning more about working at Bridgewater? Hear about the experiences of our employees  here .

About  the  Department s

Alpha Engine : The Alpha Engine is responsible for Pure Alpha, Bridgewater’s flagship alpha strategy launched in 1991. Our aim in Pure Alpha is to generate high and consistent returns, uncorrelated to markets and other managers over time. We pursue this by systematically deploying our fundamental understanding of markets and economies to trade long, short, and relative value across roughly 200 liquid public markets.

Client Investment Research within the Alpha Engine partners deeply with Pure Alpha clients and prospects on their highest-priority investment questions. We share our understanding of key dynamics driving markets and economies and advise on navigating the current market environment as well as more timeless investment challenges. Analysts also help shape how we communicate our Pure Alpha investment philosophy and process, alongside our performance and positioning amid evolving market conditions.

AIA:  What's happening in AI will likely amount to some of the most consequential technological and societal changes in modern history, and it's increasingly clear that everyone will need a plan for how to navigate them. At Bridgewater, we approach AI from two angles: as  investors  working to fully capture how AI is reshaping markets and economies, and as  practitioners  pushing the limits of what AI can do to transform how we manage money. Our central effort as practitioners is building AIA, a fully functional artificial investor designed to meet or exceed human performance across the full range of activities a human investor performs: forming views on markets, sizing positions, and revising them as conditions change. Building on the capabilities and expertise developed along the way, we are also using AI to transform our human-driven process in Pure Alpha.

Client Investment Research within AIA partners deeply with clients and prospects on how AI is reshaping markets, economies, and their portfolios. We share our understanding as both investors and practitioners: what we see in the data and what we are learning from building a fully functional artificial investor ourselves. We advise on navigating AI's implications, from exposures across markets to the broader macro environment. Analysts also help shape how we communicate Bridgewater's investment thinking on AI, our approach to managing money with it, and the lessons we are drawing as practitioners.

Strategic Investment Engine (SIE): SIE is responsible for Bridgewater’s strategic investment management, managing over $30B in long-asset strategies for many of the world’s largest and most sophisticated institutions. Our aim is to help investors achieve their long-term investment goals for compounding wealth by balancing relative and absolute return objectives. SIE deploys the same fundamental, systematic investment process that underpins all of Bridgewater’s investment strategies, applied to the particular challenge of being the ‘Best Long-Term Investor’.

Client Investment Research Associates within SIE partners deeply with Bridgewater clients and prospects on their strategic investment questions. We share our understanding of key dynamics driving portfolio outcomes and advise on ways that clients can maximize the likelihood of achieving their goals given their circumstances. Analysts also help shape how we communicate Bridgewater’s investment philosophy and process, alongside our performance and positioning amid evolving market conditions.

Asia : The goal of the Asia Strategies team is to create industry-leading portfolios and investment thinking in Asia, helping investors navigate the changing geopolitical and macroeconomic paradigm. This entails growing deep regional expertise, generating alpha in Asian markets, researching and publishing our understanding of the macroeconomic environment, and designing portfolio solutions to help our clients invest across the region.

Bridgewater has a long history as an asset manager in Asia. It started when our founder, Ray Dalio, first visited China in 1984, and we have been trading Asian markets since 1992. Asian markets have always been a core part of our global macro investment strategies, and Asian economies feature prominently in the research we have published on debt cycles and the changing world order. Bridgewater has offices in only two places – the US and Asia – reflecting the region’s strategic importance. Our first Asia-focused fund, launched in 2018, is now among the largest private funds in China.

Position Requirements

This role is designed for candidates who want to develop as investment practitioners. Deep asset management experience is not required at entry, but you should arrive with a genuine passion for markets and investing, as well as the analytical foundation for rigorous investment work.

Minimum Qualifications

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree with a strong academic and extracurricular track record

- Demonstrated interest in and understanding of markets and investing; you should have views, not just awareness

- Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, well-structured investment narratives

- Creativity and strong problem-solving instincts, including the analytical and quantitative capability to work with financial and economic data

- Intellectual curiosity about how institutional investors make decisions and how portfolios are constructed

To succeed within Bridgewater’s culture, individuals must demonstrate humility, innate curiosity, and openness to new ideas. Candidates must be driven, confident, and oriented toward self-improvement through direct feedback and honest self-reflection. All Bridgewater employees are expected to be exceptionally direct and to pursue the best answers over hierarchy, ego, or self-interest.

Physical Requirements

The anticipated onsite requirement for this role is four days per week, primarily at our New York City campus. A subset of teams operates on a hybrid schedule alternating between our New York City and Westport campuses.

Why Choose Bridgewater?

It takes all types to make Bridgewater great. We seek a diverse group of innovative thinkers and push them to engage in rigorous and thoughtful inquiry. We develop people through an honest examination of their abilities and performance, enabling personal growth and professional development. We strive to provide you with opportunities that will challenge you and unlock your potential.

Compensation Band

The wage range for this role is $130,000 – $260,000 inclusive of base salary and discretionary target bonus. The expected base salary for this role is between 70% – 80% of this wage range.

One of our core priorities at Bridgewater is to enable our employees to build a great life and career, and we believe our benefits are an important extension of that philosophy. As such, currently Bridgewater offers a competitive suite of benefits. Explore more information about Bridgewater’s benefits on our website  here.

Bridgewater reserves the right to change its current benefits program at any time, in a manner that is consistent with applicable federal and state regulations.

This job description is not a contract and confers no contractual rights, privileges, or benefits on any applicant or potential applicant. Bridgewater has the right to change any and all terms of this job description, including, but not limited to, job responsibilities, qualifications and benefits. Nothing in this job description constitutes an offer or guarantee of employment. Please note that we do provide immigration sponsorship for this position.

Bridgewater Associates, LP is an Equal Opportunity Employer

About the Investment Implementation Department
The Investment Implementation department is a community of diverse investment professionals whose mission is to implement our investment strategies and client portfolios excellently. Our Department is responsible for ensuring the excellent implementation of our systematic investment approach, from raw data to executed trades, with processes and logic that reflect the full richness of our investment insight, executed with a near-zero error rate, and engineered and orchestrated in a way that facilitates oversight and compounding. This is an investment department, owning the investment outcomes, and the mandate includes both the ‘run’ responsibility and the ‘transform’ responsibility, meaning daily operations as well as over time renovation of our systems.
We fulfill our mission by applying four operating principles:

- Understand and deliver internal client needs.  Partner with our internal clients to understand, offer implementation designs, and deliver solutions, while proactively educating and communicating outcomes to ACLs (Asset Class Leads) and CIOs.

- Own our investment intent . Own our investment intent in full, in letter and spirit.

- Continuously improve . Have and evolve an investment pipeline to meet current and future internal client needs.

- Systematically and relentlessly deliver quality outcomes . Apply our best logic systematically, discipline, expertise, and controls to every signal, position, and trade in every market

About Your Role

In this role, you will be an integral part of the Data Strategy and Acquisition function within our Investment Implementation group . O perating at the front edge of our Investment Data practice ,   y ou will  assist , learn, and contribute to the evolution of our Relationship Management, Supplier Knowledge  Management,   and  Service Management administration disciplines . You  will  engag e  with investors, associates, engineers, and external vendors and providers to drive strong outside-in and inside-out knowledge, quality management, and business process alignment .

You will be a central part of our Research and Data Strategy function   immersed in  the middle of our flows , investment questions, supplier challenges, matching ideation ,  internal marketing / advocacy, and service strategy. You will regularly communicate your understanding and assessments to a diverse group of stakeholders, including investment professionals, vendors  and service providers,  Management, Compliance, Legal, and Finance . You will  partner across the firm  and  with vendors  (existing and prospective) ,  collaborating with hundreds of individuals  (with potential to over one thousand)  over the course of a year.

You will drive the following responsibilities:

- Activating, advocating, executing, and assisting in the systems, sourcing, supply chains, and internal demand we use to provide and maintain inbound fuel and internal investment asks of the practice.

- Dynamically understanding the world of offerings, known and unknown to Bridgewater, creating potential matches, indications of interest, and bringing structure from the external world into Bridgewater.

- Understanding and effectively communicating the state of specific pieces and slices of the sourcing portfolio, including market making and matching, as well as knowledge bases of passes, no bids, and deferred opportunities.

- Assisting in the building, maintenance, and rapid sorting of inbound and run-state assets within the sourcing portfolio.

- Engaging as we rapidly introduce a ML/AI aspect to our Research and Data world discovery process designed from first principles.

- Creating and assisting in initiatives to improve the quality, reliability, and efficiency of the systems you own or are part of.

- Continuously evaluating and enhancing processes for sourcing, vetting, and delivering content to investment professionals, Data/AI scientists and processes at scale.

- Advocating with existing and potential vendors to improve the quality of their pitches.

You will be a fit for the role if you:

- Are curious, practical, analytical, and willing to engage broadly with a highly diverse set of people and processes both inside and outside of Bridgewater.

- Able to manage a high volume of work across diverse functions and competing priorities, while effectively communicating and executing.

- Are deeply interested in understanding our Investment Data practice and its lifecycle management.

- Think in terms of systems and naturally look for ways to solve problems through the evolution of those systems.

- Hold a high degree of personal responsibility and ownership in everything you do.

- Are willing to operate at all levels of the stack, from basic task execution to complex, multi-month and multi-modal efforts.

In this role, you will grow with us by:

- Undergoing a rigorous training program that includes structured engagement with the external world, on-the-job apprenticeship, and working with highly experienced colleagues.

- Actively contributing to the growth and evolution of the broader overall design.

- Having your voice and perspective heard, and over time representing the firm in important vendor, counterparty, and provider management discussions.

- Pursuing opportunities to grow your career across Bridgewater based on your strengths, areas for development, and experience

Minimum Qualifications

- 4-year degree from an accredited undergraduate institution

- 3-7 years of relevant work experience at an investment bank, vendor/service provider or asset management firm

- Experience in at least two of the following: Relationship Management, Service Management, or Supplier Knowledge Management

- Experience with Capital Markets market data is a strong plus

- Quantitative methods familiarity is a plus

Physical Requirements

The anticipated onsite requirement for this role is three days per week at our Westport, CT campus and one day per week at our NYC campus.

Compensation Band

The wage range for this role is $170,000-$225,000 inclusive of base salary and discretionary target bonus. The expected base salary for this role is between 70%-80% of this wage range.

We develop people through an honest examination of their abilities and performance, enabling personal growth and professional development. We strive to provide you with opportunities that will challenge you and unlock your potential.

Explore more information about Bridgewater’s culture on our website here .

Finance Department

Finance leads Bridgewater’s financial strategy and serves as a strategic advisor to businesses across the firm. We partner with leaders to translate strategy into financially sound plans, evaluate growth opportunities, and make informed decisions about how to allocate capital. Our work builds financial resilience and drives long-term shareholder value, supported by rigorous analysis, reporting, and controls. We are also transforming how Finance operates, using AI and automation to deliver faster insights and focus more of our expertise on the decisions that shape the firm’s future.

About the role

Finance Associates are core members of the department from day one. You will partner with leaders across the firm, build the analysis behind important decisions, and communicate the “so what” behind the numbers. Finance Associates work across areas such as business planning and analysis, corporate finance, and investor relations, gaining a broad view of how Bridgewater operates.

Every Finance Associate joins the Finance Associate Program, which helps early-career finance professionals develop, grow, and connect within Bridgewater’s Finance organization. The program has three pillars:

- Training and professional development: Training in AI, finance fundamentals, advanced Excel, and financial modeling, with a path tailored to your role.

- Mentorship and exposure to leadership: A one-on-one mentor from among Finance’s senior professionals with opportunities to learn from leaders across the organization.

- Community and cohort engagement: Join a cohort of FAs across Finance who come together to exchange ideas, learn from one another, and build relationships through discussions and events they help organize.

What You Will Do

- Build financial models and analyses that inform leadership decisions and translate insights into clear recommendations.

- Drive critical processes including planning and budgeting, financial reporting, capital planning, valuation, and liquidity analysis.

- Partner with business leaders to pressure-test decisions before resources are committed.

- Use AI tools and automation to make Finance’s work faster, more accurate, and more scalable.

- Prepare concise materials and narratives for senior leadership.

You Will Be A Fit For The Role If You Are

- Analytical: Detail-oriented and able to turn numbers into a story, separating the big from the small.

- AI-minded: Energized by using AI to redefine what finance can do, with hands-on curiosity about AI tools and large language models.

- An owner: Proactive and gritty, with the drive to carry work from idea through execution.

- An independent thinker: Comfortable using data and logic to challenge assumptions thoughtfully.

- A clear communicator: Able to explain complex ideas simply, ask sharp questions, and build trust with senior stakeholders.

- Feedback-oriented: Eager to seek and give feedback, and quick to learn from mistakes.

jobs.description:
About Bridgewater

Bridgewater Associates is a premier asset management firm, focused on delivering unique insight and partnership for the most sophisticated global institutional investors.

Our investment process is driven by a tireless pursuit to understand how the world’s markets and economies work — using cutting-edge technology to validate and execute on timeless and universal investment principles.

Founded in 1975, we are a community of independent thinkers who share a commitment to excellence. By fostering a culture of openness, transparency, and inclusion, we strive to unlock the most complex questions in investment strategy, management, and corporate culture.

Explore more information about Bridgewater on our website here .

Our Culture

Our culture is anchored in excellence, meaning constant improvement, and it is deeply tied to our mission. Because markets are objective, competitive, and getting smarter everyday, we need to keep rapidly improving to have any chance of beating them. Truth is our most essential tool for engaging with the markets and constantly improving because once you know what's true about your problems and opportunities, you can determine how to get better. Valuing truth means being transparent about your decision-making and mistakes, giving and receiving feedback with humility, and fighting for the best answers over hierarchy, ego, or self-interest. Operating this way is hard – it's only possible because we build meaning in our work and relationships. This meaning comes from the audacity of the mission, and the joy of working alongside people who make you a better version of yourself. The culture, like Bridgewater itself, is always evolving. In 1997 our founder Ray Dalio wrote down his lessons, starting with a Philosophy Statement which remains our foundation. This later evolved into a set of 300+ Principles. In 2022, when Ray transitioned the company, we re-underwrote several of those principles and evolved others, with a specific focus on Meritocracy. Today the culture sits, alongside our people, as our most important edge. When we get it right, it’s the engine that powers everything else.

Explore more information about Bridgewater’s culture on our website here .

About the Legal & Regulatory Group

The Legal & Regulatory Group is responsible for partnering with Bridgewater businesses to protect the legal and regulatory interests of the firm and its clients and managing legal and regulatory risk to ensure that employees act in accordance with the highest legal and ethical standards. Our group maintains in-house expertise in many areas, including corporate, investment management, private funds, intellectual property, employment and commercial law and compliance. The team works closely with a broad range of departments within the firm and manages relationships with external counsel and regulatory consultants.

About Your Role

The Senior Compliance Officer ("Senior Compliance Officer") will be expected to be a leader within Bridgewater's compliance function on day one. Together with other members of the team, the Senior Compliance Officer will be responsible for ensuring compliance with Bridgewater's regulatory obligations. While expected to contribute across all areas of the compliance program, the Senior Compliance Officer's primary responsibility will be owning Bridgewater's regulatory reporting and change management processes from start to finish.

This role is about doing as much as it is about thinking and advising.  The Senior Compliance Officer will be personally accountable for making sure the right filings are made accurately, excellently, and on time. Candidates should expect to spend meaningful time in the details of the filings themselves, not solely advising others on how to prepare them.

Responsibilities Include

- Preparing, reviewing, and submitting Bridgewater's regulatory filings and reports, and personally driving each one through to completion, including gathering and validating underlying data and resolving issues as they arise

- Building and running the processes, controls, and methodology used to produce accurate filings and manage regulatory interactions

- Scanning the regulatory horizon for forthcoming changes and implementing them in how filings and interactions are actually executed

- Owning quality assurance so that every filing and interaction is accurate, complete, and timely

- Advising stakeholders on their regulatory obligations and the processes used to meet them

The Senior Compliance Officer will also be expected to work with the Chief Compliance Officer ("CCO"), Deputy CCO, and other senior leaders on strategic initiatives and essential workstreams. For a high achiever, this strategic work is expected to grow over time, and ultimately the scope of the role will be limited only by the abilities and dedication of the person in it.

Minimum Qualifications

- 7-10 years of legal and/or compliance experience with a focus on regulatory reporting for asset managers and private funds

- Ownership mindset and good judgment; the willingness and capability to work tirelessly with the intellect and judgment to make that needed only sparingly

- Familiarity with regulations applicable to alternative investment managers and private funds

- High intellectual horsepower, agility, logical reasoning, practicality and curiosity

- Comfort operating proactively and independently while simultaneously not being afraid to ask for help

- Basic comfort with data and able to work with spreadsheets/databases to identify patterns or anomalies

- Thrives in a fast-paced environment; comfortable juggling priorities and escalating when at risk of failure

- Strong project management and oversight capabilities; willingness to hold others accountable to deadlines and obligations

- Comfort learning and adopting new software/AI tools quickly, with genuine interest in how technology can improve compliance processes

- Strong interpersonal skills; professional, team-oriented with strong work ethic and a “can-do, will-do” attitude

- Excellent oral and written communication skills

- Excellent organizational and time management skill with a strong attention to detail

Physical Requirements

The onsite requirement for this role is four days per week at our Westport, CT campus, with occasional travel to our NYC campus as needed.

Compensation

The wage range for this role is $260,000 - $480,000 inclusive of base salary and discretionary target bonus. The expected base salary for this role is between 65% - 75% of this wage range.

Why Choose Bridgewater?

It takes all types to make Bridgewater great. We seek a diverse group of innovative thinkers and push them to engage in rigorous and thoughtful inquiry. We develop people through an honest examination of their abilities and performance, enabling personal growth and professional development. We strive to provide you with opportunities that will challenge you and unlock your potential.

One of our core priorities at Bridgewater is to enable our employees to build a great life and career, and we believe our benefits are an important extension of that philosophy. As such, currently Bridgewater offers a competitive suite of benefits. Explore more information about Bridgewater’s benefits on our website here.

The Finance Department

Finance leads Bridgewater’s financial strategy and serves as a strategic advisor to businesses across the firm. We partner with leaders to translate strategy into financially sound plans, evaluate growth opportunities, and make informed decisions about how to allocate capital. Our work builds financial resilience and drives long-term shareholder value, supported by rigorous analysis, reporting, and controls. We are also transforming how Finance operates, using AI and automation to deliver faster insights and focus more of our expertise on the decisions that shape the firm’s future.

About the Role:

As a Senior Finance Associate on Bridgewater's Corporate Accounting team, your primary responsibility will be the accounting and reporting of the Company’s expanding foreign operations, reporting to the Controller responsible for that area. Additionally, you will provide leverage to the Head of Accounting Policy and Reporting by performing technical accounting analyses and supporting the financial reporting process for the Company’s domestic entities. You will help lead how we use process change and technology to make reporting and accounting sharper, faster and better controlled. This is a highly visible role that will put you in direct contact with external auditors, third-party service providers, and stakeholders across the Finance Department. You will develop a diversified skill set and breadth of knowledge that are highly valued across the firm.

You will drive the following responsibilities:

Under the supervision of the Controller responsible for the accounting and reporting of our foreign subsidiaries:

- Project manage the annual audits of these entities’ statutory financial statements, which are prepared under local statutory GAAP (IFRS based)

- Serve as a primary point of contact for the external auditors, resolving requests and comments directly where appropriate and coordinating input from others across the organization as necessary

- Ensure that transactions are accounted for (both technically and operationally) and reported on correctly. For subsidiaries in which we use external service providers to prepare monthly and annual reporting packages (trial balance, account reconciliations, balance sheet, profit and loss statement, cash flow statement, and related schedules), review their work critically for accuracy, completeness and appropriate accounting treatment and ensure it is appropriately loaded into our general ledger

- Field questions from and proactively raise accounting issues with the Business Planning and Analysis team responsible for our foreign subsidiaries

- Actively incorporate AI tooling to enable and streamline processes, helping to push the efficiency of existing work streams while reimagining how they get done

While the accounting and reporting of our foreign operations will be your primary responsibility, you will also have the opportunity to support the Head of Accounting Policy and Reporting with accounting policy and reporting needs, such as performing technical accounting analyses of new transactions (US GAAP), creating new accounting policies and/or updating existing policies, and adopting/implementing new accounting standards. Further, you may be asked to support the quarterly and annual financial reporting process for our domestic operations.

You will be a click for the role if you:

- Possess an exceptional ownership mentality, willing to roll up your sleeves and problem solve

- Can proactively and independently use AI fluently in your work while bringing enough technical depth of your own to review its output for accuracy and completeness

- Are a capable project manager who can drive to deadlines and hold stakeholders accountable without relying on formal authority

- Have a genuine appetite for rethinking how the work gets done — questioning processes and tools and pushing for better, better-controlled ways to account and report, rather than settling for incremental tweaks

- Show strong critical thinking skills, with a natural curiosity to ask "why" and question the status quo

- Enjoy making sense out of white-space and ambiguous situations

- Think analytically, logically and agilely; can quickly iterate in a fast-paced environment and high-performance culture

- Excel at relationship building across stakeholders at all levels of the Company, as well as with external auditors and third-party service providers

- Are highly organized, reliable and detail oriented, with an eye for spotting and correcting errors

We are looking for candidates with the following minimum qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree or higher in accounting, with a strong academic track record

- 5-7 years of accounting or audit experience, ideally with hands-on exposure to project management and to coordinating across teams to get things done; Big 4 background a plus

- CPA or actively working towards the certification

- Experience in operational accounting, including processes and controls

- A solid understanding of how financial statements are assembled and experience working within draft statements to get them right

- Experience working with AI tooling, paired with the subject matter expertise to review AI-generated output for accuracy and completeness (we currently use Claude, though our tooling may change over time)

- Solid technical accounting skills (i.e., the ability to research an accounting question and reach a supportable, well-documented conclusion)

- Advanced Excel skills

- Experience with other financial systems, such as Workday, Office Connect or Power Query preferred

Physical Requirements

The onsite requirement for this role is four days per week at our Westport, CT headquarters campus.

Compensation

The wage range for this role is $165K-$235K inclusive of base salary and discretionary target bonus. The expected base salary for this role is between 80% - 90% of this wage range.
